summary:
### TL;DR
- Copilot code review settings can now be managed through the REST and GraphQL APIs at the enterprise, organization, and repository levels. New attribution fields identify Copilot's reviews and comments. Enterprise and organization endpoints don't accept GitHub Apps or fine-grained PATs. ([changelog](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-06-copilot-code-review-api-management-and-review-overview-updates))
- GitHub Actions, Dependabot, and org- or enterprise-owned apps can again request Copilot reviews on bot-authored PRs when "Block reviews requested with an external Copilot license" is on, as long as the org pays for the review. ([changelog](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-06-copilot-code-review-api-management-and-review-overview-updates))
- The Actions limits docs now list the self-hosted runner registration limit (1500 runners / 5 minutes) as **not** increasable. Previously it could be raised through a Support ticket. ([docs](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/limits))
- The AI push protection docs now explain who is billed for AI credit usage. ([docs](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/how-tos/secure-your-secrets/prevent-future-leaks/enable-ai-push-protection))

### Action required
There are no dated deprecations or breaking changes this time. Two items to plan for:
- **Self-hosted runner scaling:** You can no longer get the runner registration limit (1500 runners / 5 minutes per repository, org, or enterprise) raised through a Support ticket. Teams with bursty autoscaling should design within this limit. ([docs](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/limits), [commit](https://github.com/github/docs/commit/c23840f12a2e6e1cf6b405699f05319cb46190c0))
- **Automation tokens for Copilot code review settings:** Choose credentials based on the endpoint level. ([changelog](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-06-copilot-code-review-api-management-and-review-overview-updates))
  - Enterprise and organization endpoints, including the org runner endpoint, do not support GitHub Apps or fine-grained PATs.
  - Repository endpoints support both. They need Administration: read to read settings and Administration: write to update them.
  - Classic PATs need repository admin access.

### Security improvements
- **Attribution and provenance for Copilot reviews:** Explicit attribution fields identify Copilot's reviews and comments in the API. You can also see which skills, MCP servers, and custom instructions Copilot reported as sources for a comment. ([changelog](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-06-copilot-code-review-api-management-and-review-overview-updates))
- **Policy hierarchy enforcement:** Organizations can't override code review settings managed by the enterprise. Repository admins can control whether reviews use custom instructions and MCP tools. ([changelog](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-06-copilot-code-review-api-management-and-review-overview-updates))
- **Ruleset bypass support:** The "Automatically request Copilot code review" repository rule now honors the bypass list. Exempt actors won't get automatic reviews. ([changelog](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-06-copilot-code-review-api-management-and-review-overview-updates))
- **Bot-authored PR reviews restored:** Actions, Dependabot, and owned apps can again request reviews on bot-authored PRs when external-license blocking is enabled, provided the org pays for the review. ([changelog](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-06-copilot-code-review-api-management-and-review-overview-updates))
- **Assisted tool approval in the Copilot app:** You can now give Copilot opt-in personal instructions on which tool requests to approve without asking you. These apply to local sessions only. Review this against your org's policies for agent autonomy. ([changelog](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-06-github-copilot-weekly-releases-november-2))

### Docs changes worth reading
- **[Enable AI push protection](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/how-tos/secure-your-secrets/prevent-future-leaks/enable-ai-push-protection)** ([commit](https://github.com/github/docs/commit/824e8a77f466a43f2f62e2b148deb31f22a8475a)): The page now states how AI credit usage is billed.
  - Usage is billed to the organization that owns the repository.
  - For organization-owned repos in an enterprise, usage counts toward the enterprise's AI credit pool.
  - Only repos in a managed user's personal namespace consume the owner's individual pool, regardless of who pushes. Otherwise, individual pools are not charged.
- **[Actions limits](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/limits)** ([commit](https://github.com/github/docs/commit/c23840f12a2e6e1cf6b405699f05319cb46190c0)): The self-hosted runner registration limit changed from "increase via Support ticket" to "No," so it can't be raised.

changelog.title: Copilot code review: API management and review overview updates
changelog.text: You can now manage GitHub Copilot code review settings through the REST and GraphQL APIs, from enterprise policy down to individual repositories. Copilot’s review overview comment is now more compact, and this update includes fixes for billing, automatic reviews, and reliability. These updates are available to Copilot Pro, Pro+, Max, Business, and Enterprise plans. 🔌 Manage settings and identify Copilot’s output through the API You can already request reviews, choose their effort level, and get information back through the REST API. You can now also: Identify Copilot’s reviews and comments through explicit attribution fields. See the review effort a review used, when that metadata is available. See which skills, MCP servers, and custom instructions Copilot reported as sources for a comment. Depending on your role, you can also read and update code review settings: Enterprise administrators can enable or disable code review for all organizations, or leave the choice to organization administrators. Organization administrators can manage code review enablement, the default review effort, and the runner configuration. Settings your enterprise manages can’t be overridden. Repository administrators can manage review effort and whether reviews use custom instructions and MCP tools. The REST API accepts the same review effort levels as the web interface, and organization and repository settings responses list the levels available to you. ⚠️ The enterprise and organization settings endpoints, including the organization runner endpoint, don’t support GitHub Apps or fine-grained personal access tokens. The repository settings endpoints support both, with Administration: read permission to read settings and Administration: write permission to update them. Classic personal access tokens need repository administrator access. To get started, see Configuring Copilot code review with the API . 📋 A more compact review overview New review overviews keep your findings together at the top: The review effort used and any surveys move into a compact footer. Skipped and content-excluded files share one “Files not reviewed” section, with filenames and linked exclusion reasons. Empty sections are left out, and long lists show an overflow count. You can also tell us what’s wrong with an overview. After you give it a 👎, choose Add a reason and pick the main problem, such as an approval assessment you disagree with, a comment that’s too verbose, or findings that are incorrect or nitpicky. We use this feedback to improve Copilot’s findings. ✨ Other improvements Copilot code review agent sessions now show the AI credits consumed in a review. The Automatically request Copilot code review repository rule now supports the bypass list, so exempt actors in the list will not receive an automatic review from Copilot. Copilot code review organization and repository settings pages have clearer wording and layout. On later reviews of the same pull request, findings unrelated to your recent changes are collapsed and then hidden. Balanced effort reviews now use three reviewer models, with another model combining their findings. 🐛 Bug fixes Billing and preview settings are now preserved when you turn code review off and on again. Failed or timed-out reviews are retried once automatically, and Copilot can switch to another eligible model when the preferred one is unavailable. GitHub Actions, Dependabot, and apps your organization or enterprise owns can request reviews on bot-authored pull requests again when Block reviews requested with an external Copilot license is on, as long as your organization pays for the review. Reviews no longer report a false failure just after starting and discard their results. Reviews in progress during a service update now get more time to finish. Review surveys no longer appear when your organization has opted out of feedback collection. The post Copilot code review: API management and review overview updates appeared first on The GitHub B

changelog.title: GitHub Copilot weekly releases — November 2
changelog.text: This week, Copilot comes to JetBrains Air and Xcode’s coding assistant, with updates to help you manage pull requests, settings, and agent sessions. GitHub Copilot app Set up Agent Merge directly from a pull request to have Copilot merge it when it’s ready. It now stays enabled while required checks or rules are pending. You can also check reviewer status, request additional reviews, and select comment text to quote it or discuss it with Copilot. Keep working when a conversation reaches its context limit. Compact the conversation or review what’s using the available space directly from the error. Start a session by dropping files on “New” in the sidebar. CSV and TSV files now open as tables with sticky headers and an option to view the source. Manage sessions in fewer steps. Archive pinned sessions whose pull requests have merged or closed, pin or unpin multiple sessions, and separate nested chats without losing the conversation. My Work now supports more than ten saved custom views. Give Copilot guidance on which tool requests to approve without asking you. Personal instructions for assisted approval are opt-in and apply to local sessions. Install the GitHub Copilot app . GitHub Copilot CLI Manage your whole setup in one place. /settings now opens a unified dashboard for your plugins, MCP servers, and more, and you can search across all of your settings. Install Copilot CLI . GitHub Copilot in JetBrains Introducing a new way to use GitHub Copilot in JetBrains IDEs, with Copilot now available in JetBrains Air. Track multiple agent sessions and run tasks locally in your JetBrains IDE or in the cloud through Air Teams, using your existing Copilot subscription. Get started with Copilot in JetBrains Air . GitHub Copilot in Xcode You can now work with GitHub Copilot directly in Xcode’s built-in coding assistant, bringing Copilot into your native Xcode workflow. The integration is now in public preview, available starting with Xcode 27.3 beta. Get started with Copilot in Xcode . GitHub Copilot in VS Code (1.145 release) Follow the conversation without the clutter or, alternatively, choose to inspect every step. Experimental chat view modes let you collapse or expand reasoning and tool calls without starting a new conversation. Check an agent’s work on another machine without leaving VS Code. Preview remote apps and use interactive canvases in the Agents window, now in preview. Enable remote browser support in settings, plus canvases to use that feature. Run recurring tasks on a schedule that fits your workflow. Local automations now support cron expressions and custom agents from your workspace. Bring screenshots, mockups, and other files into chat without moving them into your workspace. Choose them with Add Context > Files . Cloud sessions only support images. Get back into long Copilot chats more smoothly. Past terminal output now renders as you expand or reveal it instead of loading all at once. Explore everything that’s new in the full release notes . The post GitHub Copilot weekly releases — November 2 appeared first on The GitHub Blog .
